from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # --- Data Setup ---
        title_text = "The Core Concept: Updating Beliefs"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Probability is your degree of belief in an event.",
            "New evidence should change how you view the world.",
            "This update is the heart of Bayes' Theorem."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color1 = "#ADD8E6"  # Light Blue
        color2 = "#32CD32"  # Lime Green
        color3 = "#FF4500"  # Orange Red

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color1))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # Display the text 'Probability: Your Degree of Belief' in #ADD8E6.
        belief_text = Text("Probability: Your Degree of Belief", font_size=24, color=color1)
        self.place_in_area(belief_text, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(belief_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color2)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # Create a meter showing a '20% Chance of Rain' (#32CD32).
        meter_bg = Rectangle(width=4, height=0.5, color=WHITE)
        # 20% of 4 units is 0.8 units wide
        meter_fill = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=color2, stroke_width=0)
        meter_fill.align_to(meter_bg, LEFT)
        meter_group = VGroup(meter_bg, meter_fill)
        self.place_at_grid(meter_group, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        rain_label = Text("20% Chance of Rain", font_size=22, color=color2)
        self.place_at_grid(rain_label, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(meter_bg), FadeIn(meter_fill), Write(rain_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color3)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # Update the meter to 69% as dark clouds appear (#FF4500).
        # Dark clouds (simple geometric representation using grey circles)
        cloud_circles = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.3, fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#808080", stroke_width=0),
            Circle(radius=0.4, fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#808080", stroke_width=0).shift(RIGHT * 0.4),
            Circle(radius=0.3, fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#808080", stroke_width=0).shift(RIGHT * 0.8)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(cloud_circles, "C5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # 69% of 4 units is 2.76 units wide
        new_meter_fill = Rectangle(width=4 * 0.69, height=0.5, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=color3, stroke_width=0)
        new_meter_fill.align_to(meter_bg, LEFT)
        
        new_rain_label = Text("69% Chance of Rain", font_size=22, color=color3)
        self.place_at_grid(new_rain_label, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cloud_circles))
        self.play(
            Transform(meter_fill, new_meter_fill),
            Transform(rain_label, new_rain_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: The Probability Square"
        lines = [
            "Imagine all possibilities fitting inside a unit square.",
            "The square's total area represents absolute certainty.",
            "Your initial belief is a portion of this space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1.5) # [L010]
        
        # Draw a white 1x1 square representing all possibilities (#FFFFFF).
        # We use a 3x3 area in the grid to represent the square.
        # Grid range B2 to E5 gives a nice square area.
        unit_square = Square(side_length=3.0, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(unit_square, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        self.play(Create(unit_square))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 2
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1.5) # [L010]
        
        # The square's total area represents absolute certainty.
        # Pulse the square to emphasize total area.
        self.play(Indicate(unit_square, color="#FFFFFF")) # [L004]
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 3 - Blue to match the "Prior" column
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        self.wait(1.5) # [L010]
        
        # Shade a blue vertical column for 20% 'Prior' probability (#0000FF).
        # Since the square width is 3.0, 20% is 0.6.
        prior_width = 3.0 * 0.2
        prior_rect = Rectangle(
            width=prior_width, 
            height=3.0, 
            fill_color="#0000FF", 
            fill_opacity=0.5, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        # Position the rect on the left side of the square.
        # Square center is at (3.0, -0.3).
        # Left edge of square is at 3.0 - 1.5 = 1.5.
        # Rect center should be at 1.5 + (prior_width / 2) = 1.5 + 0.3 = 1.8.
        prior_rect.move_to(unit_square.get_left() + RIGHT * (prior_width / 2))
        
        # Add a label 'P(Rain) = 0.2' inside the blue column (#FFFFFF).
        # [L002] Scale labels 0.7-0.8 and place within 1 grid unit.
        prior_label = MathTex("P(\\text{Rain}) = 0.2", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24)
        # Scaled per [L002]
        prior_label.scale(0.8)
        
        # Place label near the column. Since the column is narrow, 
        # we can place it slightly to the right or centered if it fits.
        # For a 0.6 width rect, a 0.8 scale label might be tight. 
        # Let's rotate it or place it just above/beside.
        # Storyboard says "inside the blue column".
        # Let's check if it fits. 
        # Width of "P(Rain) = 0.2" at font_size 24 is roughly 1-1.5 units? 
        # 0.6 is quite narrow. Let's use a vertical label or place it at C2/C3.
        
        # Actually, let's just place it at grid 'C2' which is near the left of the square.
        # B2 is (1.5, 1.2), C2 is (2.5, 1.2).
        self.place_at_grid(prior_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prior_rect))
        self.play(Write(prior_label))
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Prior and the Likelihood (The Slicing)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We start with the probability of rain.",
            "This 'Prior' is represented by a vertical column.",
            "Next, we consider how often evidence occurs.",
            "A horizontal slice represents the likelihood of a beep.",
            "This creates specific regions for rain and no rain."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Establish the 1x1 probability square using a 3x3 square in the grid space
        square_size = 3.0
        rain_width = square_size * 0.2
        no_rain_width = square_size * 0.8
        
        # Main square border
        sq_border = Rectangle(width=square_size, height=square_size, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Rain column (Prior)
        rain_col = Rectangle(
            width=rain_width, height=square_size, 
            fill_color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=1
        )
        rain_col.align_to(sq_border, LEFT)
        
        # No Rain column
        no_rain_col = Rectangle(
            width=no_rain_width, height=square_size, 
            fill_color="#888888", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=1
        )
        no_rain_col.align_to(sq_border, RIGHT)
        
        # Group and place
        prob_space = VGroup(sq_border, rain_col, no_rain_col)
        self.place_in_area(prob_space, "B2", "E5")

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.play(Create(sq_border), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(rain_col), FadeIn(no_rain_col))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Prior Label
        prior_label = Text("P(Rain) = 0.2", font_size=20, color="#0000FF").scale(0.8)
        prior_label.next_to(rain_col, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.play(Write(prior_label))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        # Absorption time before introducing Likelihood
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Horizontal slices for likelihood: P(Beep|Rain)=0.9, P(Beep|NoRain)=0.1
        tp_height = square_size * 0.9
        fp_height = square_size * 0.1
        
        tp_slice = Line(
            start=rain_col.get_bottom() + UP * tp_height + LEFT * rain_width/2,
            end=rain_col.get_bottom() + UP * tp_height + RIGHT * rain_width/2,
            color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4
        )
        fp_slice = Line(
            start=no_rain_col.get_bottom() + UP * fp_height + LEFT * no_rain_width/2,
            end=no_rain_col.get_bottom() + UP * fp_height + RIGHT * no_rain_width/2,
            color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4
        )
        
        # Label the horizontal slices
        likelihood_label = Text("Likelihood: P(Evidence | Event)", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(likelihood_label, "A4", scale_factor=0.8) # Near the top of the square area
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(Create(tp_slice), Create(fp_slice))
        self.play(Write(likelihood_label))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlighted regions (Intersections)
        rain_beep_rect = Rectangle(
            width=rain_width, height=tp_height,
            fill_color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        rain_beep_rect.align_to(rain_col, DOWN).align_to(rain_col, LEFT)
        
        no_rain_beep_rect = Rectangle(
            width=no_rain_width, height=fp_height,
            fill_color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        no_rain_beep_rect.align_to(no_rain_col, DOWN).align_to(no_rain_col, LEFT)
        
        # Region labels
        tp_tag = Text("True Pos", font_size=16, color="#00FF00").scale(0.7)
        fp_tag = Text("False Pos", font_size=16, color="#FF0000").scale(0.7)
        
        # Proximity placement (L002)
        tp_tag.next_to(rain_beep_rect, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        fp_tag.next_to(no_rain_beep_rect, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(rain_beep_rect), FadeIn(no_rain_beep_rect))
        self.play(Write(tp_tag), Write(fp_tag))
        self.wait(3.0)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # === Setup ===
        title = "The Geometry of Evidence (Filtering)"
        lines = [
            "Evidence has arrived: the sensor just beeped.",
            "We discard all regions where no beep occurred.",
            "Only the \"Beep\" rectangles remain in our view."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_TP = "#00FF00"  # Green: Rain + Beep
        COLOR_FP = "#FF0000"  # Red: No Rain + Beep
        COLOR_DIM = "#555555"
        COLOR_BG = "#333333"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"

        # Geometry parameters (normalized to 3.0 units total square)
        W_TOTAL = 3.5
        H_TOTAL = 3.5
        P_RAIN = 0.3
        P_BEEP_RAIN = 0.8
        P_BEEP_NORAIN = 0.2
        
        w_rain = W_TOTAL * P_RAIN
        w_norain = W_TOTAL * (1 - P_RAIN)
        
        h_beep_rain = H_TOTAL * P_BEEP_RAIN
        h_nobeep_rain = H_TOTAL * (1 - P_BEEP_RAIN)
        
        h_beep_norain = H_TOTAL * P_BEEP_NORAIN
        h_nobeep_norain = H_TOTAL * (1 - P_BEEP_NORAIN)

        # Create Rectangles
        # TP: Rain + Beep
        rect_tp = Rectangle(width=w_rain, height=h_beep_rain, fill_color=COLOR_TP, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=2)
        # FN: Rain + No Beep
        rect_fn = Rectangle(width=w_rain, height=h_nobeep_rain, fill_color=COLOR_BG, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        # FP: No Rain + Beep
        rect_fp = Rectangle(width=w_norain, height=h_beep_norain, fill_color=COLOR_FP, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=2)
        # TN: No Rain + No Beep
        rect_tn = Rectangle(width=w_norain, height=h_nobeep_norain, fill_color=COLOR_BG, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)

        # Alignment logic (forming the full square)
        # Column 1 (Rain)
        rect_tp.move_to(ORIGIN) # temporary
        rect_fn.next_to(rect_tp, DOWN, buff=0)
        
        # Column 2 (No Rain)
        # We align the top edge of FP with the top edge of TP to make a consistent "Beep" row?
        # Actually, standard grid Bayes is: TP and FP are at the top.
        rect_fp.align_to(rect_tp, UP).next_to(rect_tp, RIGHT, buff=0)
        rect_tn.next_to(rect_fp, DOWN, buff=0)

        # Create the full square group and center it in the area
        full_square = VGroup(rect_tp, rect_fn, rect_fp, rect_tn)
        self.place_in_area(full_square, "B2", "E5")

        # Initial Labels (optional for context, matching storyboard 'Beep' focus)
        label_rain = Text("Rain", font_size=18).scale(0.8)
        label_norain = Text("No Rain", font_size=18).scale(0.8)
        
        # Position labels above the columns (A2-A4 area roughly)
        label_rain.next_to(rect_tp, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_norain.next_to(rect_fp, UP, buff=0.2)

        self.add(full_square, label_rain, label_norain)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Evidence has arrived: the sensor just beeped."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Dim parts except intersections (TP and FP represent 'Beep')
        self.play(
            rect_fn.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DIM, opacity=0.4).set_stroke(COLOR_DIM),
            rect_tn.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DIM, opacity=0.4).set_stroke(COLOR_DIM),
            Indicate(rect_tp, color=COLOR_TP),
            Indicate(rect_fp, color=COLOR_FP),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We discard all regions where no beep occurred."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Remove dimmed areas and labels
        self.play(
            FadeOut(rect_fn),
            FadeOut(rect_tn),
            FadeOut(label_rain),
            FadeOut(label_norain),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Only the \"Beep\" rectangles remain in our view."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Move remaining rectangles to center. 
        # They are currently aligned by their tops but separate widths.
        # We'll group them and center them.
        beep_group = VGroup(rect_tp, rect_fp)
        
        # Create descriptive labels for the remaining areas
        text_tp = Text("True Positive", font_size=16, color=COLOR_TP).scale(0.8)
        text_fp = Text("False Positive", font_size=16, color=COLOR_FP).scale(0.8)
        
        text_tp.next_to(rect_tp, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        text_fp.next_to(rect_fp, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Centering the remaining evidence
        target_center_pos = self.grid["C3"] + RIGHT * 0.5 # Shift slightly right for balance

        self.play(
            beep_group.animate.move_to(target_center_pos),
            Write(text_tp),
            Write(text_fp),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Final emphasis
        self.play(
            Indicate(text_tp),
            Indicate(text_fp),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines and title
        title = "Summary and Intuition Check"
        lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem turns evidence into updated knowledge.",
            "We filter the world through what we observe.",
            "Now you can update your mind with geometric precision."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_METER = "#32CD32"
        COLOR_CALC = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_TAKEAWAY = "#FFD700"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Cloud-Bot meter jump 20% to 69%
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_METER)
        
        # Meter Mobjects
        meter_width = 3.0
        meter_height = 0.6
        
        meter_bg = Rectangle(width=meter_width, height=meter_height, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        meter_fill = Rectangle(
            width=meter_width * 0.20, 
            height=meter_height, 
            fill_opacity=0.8, 
            fill_color=COLOR_METER, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        meter_fill.align_to(meter_bg, LEFT)
        
        meter_group = VGroup(meter_bg, meter_fill)
        self.place_in_area(meter_group, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        belief_label = Text("Rain Probability", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        belief_label.next_to(meter_group, UP, buff=0.3)
        
        percent_val = ValueTracker(20)
        percent_text = DecimalNumber(20, unit="%", num_decimal_places=0, color="#FFFFFF")
        percent_text.scale(0.8)
        percent_text.next_to(meter_group, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Meter Updater
        def update_meter(m):
            new_width = meter_width * (percent_val.get_value() / 100)
            if new_width < 0.01: new_width = 0.01
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(new_width, about_edge=LEFT)
            
        meter_fill.add_updater(update_meter)
        percent_text.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(percent_val.get_value()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(meter_group), FadeIn(belief_label), FadeIn(percent_text))
        self.wait(1.5) # Absorption time
        
        # Update belief
        self.play(
            percent_val.animate.set_value(69),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=bezier([0, 0, 1, 1])
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Calculation: '0.18 divided by 0.26 equals 0.69'
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_CALC)
        
        calc_tex = MathTex(
            r"\frac{0.18}{0.26} \approx 0.69",
            color=COLOR_CALC
        )
        self.place_at_grid(calc_tex, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.wait(1.5)
        self.play(Write(calc_tex))
        self.play(Indicate(calc_tex, color=COLOR_CALC))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight takeaway: 'Evidence updates belief through geometry'
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_TAKEAWAY)
        
        takeaway = Text("Evidence updates belief\nthrough geometry", font_size=24, color=COLOR_TAKEAWAY, line_spacing=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(takeaway, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.wait(1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(takeaway, shift=UP*0.3))
        self.play(Indicate(takeaway, color=COLOR_TAKEAWAY))
        
        # Final highlight of all elements
        self.play(
            Circumscribe(meter_group, color=COLOR_METER),
            Circumscribe(calc_tex, color=COLOR_CALC),
            Circumscribe(takeaway, color=COLOR_TAKEAWAY),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Changing Your Mind
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with basic algebra knowledge.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Updating Beliefs
sections.content: Introduce the idea that probability isn't just a fixed number, but a 'degree of belief' that should change when new evidence arrives. Define the transition from Prior Belief to Posterior Belief.
sections.example: A 'Cloud-Bot' robot predicts rain. Initially, it thinks there is a 20% chance of rain (Prior). Suddenly, it sees dark clouds (Evidence). How much should its belief increase?

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Probability Square
sections.content: Establish a geometric foundation. Visualize the total probability space as a 1x1 square with an area of 1. Any event is represented as a sub-area within this square.
sections.example: Draw a 1x1 square. If the 'Prior' probability of rain is 0.2, shade a vertical column representing 20% of the square's total area.

sections.title: The Prior and the Likelihood (The Slicing)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Likelihood'—the probability of the evidence occurring given the event. In the square, this is represented by a horizontal slice that intersects our prior area.
sections.example: Suppose the 'Cloud-Bot' sensor beeps 90% of the time when it actually rains (True Positive), but also 10% of the time when it's sunny (False Positive). We slice the 'Rain' column at 0.9 height and the 'No Rain' column at 0.1 height.

sections.title: The Geometry of Evidence (Filtering)
sections.content: When the evidence (the beep) happens, all areas of the square where the evidence *doesn't* happen become irrelevant. We 'throw away' the parts of the square that don't match the observation.
sections.example: The screen dims the areas where the sensor stayed silent. We are left with two small rectangles: The 'True Positive' area (Rain + Beep) and the 'False Positive' area (No Rain + Beep).

sections.title: Normalization: The New Universe
sections.content: Explain that because the remaining areas must now represent the 'new' total certainty (100%), we must rescale/zoom into these remaining slivers so their sum area equals 1 again.
sections.example: Visually 'stretch' the remaining 'Beep' rectangles vertically until they fill the 1x1 square again. The ratio of the 'Rain' sliver to the 'Total Beep' area is the new probability.

sections.title: The Formal Formula (The Mathematical Map)
sections.content: Map the geometric actions (Slicing and Rescaling) to the formal algebraic notation of Bayes' Theorem: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B).
sections.example: Show that P(A) is the width of our initial column, P(B|A) is the height of our slice, and P(B) is the total area remaining after the evidence filter.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition Check
sections.content: Recap that Bayes' Theorem is simply a way of calculating 'the area of the target event' divided by 'the total area of all events that could have caused the evidence.'
sections.example: Animate the Cloud-Bot updating its internal meter from 20% to approximately 69% based on the geometric ratio we just calculated.
